newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut oil prices seen steady on lack of factors.
newsitem.headline: Coconut oil prices seen steady on lack of factors.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to trade sideways this week due to lack of market-moving factors, Manila vegetable oil traders said on Monday.

"Coconut oil volume from the Philippines will remain limited compared to market requirement. But I expect Indonesia to continue filling up the shortfall of the Philippine exports," a senior Manila trader told Reuters.
Indonesia last month exported an estimated 50,000 to 55,000 tonnes of coconut oil.

Philippine coconut oil exports in the first two months of the year increased to 142,200 tonnes from the year-ago 137,699 tonnes, trade group United Coconut Association of the Philippines said last week. UCAP said the figures were preliminary.
"I expect prices to remain in a narrow range until Indonesian export tapers," said one trader.
Traders said they do not expect much demand this week because buyers have bought enough in the past weeks when stocks were high.
Stocks in Rotterdam dropped to 16,826 tonnes as of March 3 as against the 19,263 tonnes on February 24.
Prices last week softened between $10 and $15 per tonne due to improved weather conditions in coconut growing areas in the Philippines, traders said.
